_comment: What the three children are DOING in a scene. Supplied by the household 2026-09-02, with
the instruction that they must not always be doing the same thing — the first scenes had
flowers / marshmallow / scooter welded to slots 1 / 2 / 0 and every picture repeated it.
THIS FILE REPLACED A CONVENTION, AND THE CONVENTION HAD A REASON. assets/scenes/*.json used
to say that slots keep the same activity across scenes 'because the pre-reader finds herself
by look and position, and a scene change that also moves everyone would make her hunt
again'. That trade is now made the other way ON PURPOSE: hunting is the POINT of a
search-and-find picture, and the identity channel that survives is the one that was always
doing the work — hair and garment colour, which are pinned by the portraits and unchanged.
`solo` entries are drawn per child. `shared` entries put two or three of them in one
activity together, which is the thing the old structure could not express at all.
`seasons` is a filter, not a promise: an empty list means any time of year. The scheduler
picks activities that suit the setting and the weather, so 'sledding' and 'lake' are not
offered in the same week.
SHARED ACTIVITIES FIGHT THE TAP GUTTER, and the refusal is what mediates it. 'all three
sitting in a row on a fallen log' put them 1px and 4px apart on 2026-09-03 — no overlap, but
well under the 16px inert gutter two tap targets need, so scene-regions.py refused the whole
scene. That is the system working: a re-roll costs $0.14 and a wrong tap costs a child
opening her sibling's screen. gen-scene.py now asks for a whole child's width between them,
which helps; entries that seat them in a row will still refuse more often than the rest.
`family` STOPS TWO CHILDREN DOING THE SAME KIND OF THING. Three of the twenty-one solo
entries are animal-riding, so an unconstrained sample of three drew one child on a bear and
another on an elk in the same picture — which reads as the generator having one idea rather
than as three children with three ideas. pick_activities() now takes at most one entry per
family, which is also why the list wants breadth of KIND rather than more entries of a kind
already covered.
EVERY ENTRY NAMES ITS PLACES, AND THERE IS NO 'ANYWHERE' (2026-10-04). `settings` used to be
allowed empty, meaning 'fits anywhere', and a setting with empty `tags` admitted every row —
both on purpose, so that nothing untagged could ever produce an empty menu. What it produced
instead was a deer ride and a tree climb inside a school library: the outdoor table carried
forward into a room it was never written for, and nothing said so until the picture came back.
The filter fails CLOSED now. `places` below is the whole vocabulary; an entry with no places,
a setting with no tags, or a tag outside the list is refused by `scene-week.check_tables()`
before anything is paid for, and so is any setting that cannot fill three different KINDS of
activity in every season it is drawn in. tools/scene_activities.py is the one definition.

riding on the back of a big gentle bear
riding on the back of a friendly elk
holding a bird that has landed on their hands
balancing along a low wall or a log with both arms out
throwing a ball

riding a bicycle
flying a kite on a long string
climbing high in the branches of a tree
sitting on a branch reading a book
splashing at the edge of the water
building a snowman
pulling a sledge up a slope
jumping in a puddle in wellington boots
carrying a lantern along a path
toasting a marshmallow over a campfire
picking wildflowers
riding a scooter along a path
pulling a book down from a high shelf, up on a little step stool
curled up in a big beanbag with a picture book open on their knees
building a tall wobbly tower out of wooden blocks
painting a picture at a little wooden easel
pushing a little wooden trolley loaded with books
playing a small drum
eating a big ice-cream cone

carrying a pumpkin almost too big to hold
skating in little circles on the ice
jumping off the side of the pool feet-first, mid-air above the water

sitting on the edge of the pool, kicking their feet and splashing

shared.do: {all_of_them} building a den out of long sticks together
{all_of_them} sitting in a row on a fallen log
two of them carrying a big basket between them while the third runs ahead
{all_of_them} in a rowing boat on the water
two of them on a see-saw while the third pushes a swing
{all_of_them} lying on their fronts looking into a rock pool
two of them carrying a tall stack of books between them while the third leads the way
{all_of_them} sitting in a row on the pool edge with their feet in the water

places.meadow: open grass, a lawn or a hillside
places.park: a playground, a green or a garden
places.lake: the shore of still fresh water
places.town: streets, a market or a village lane
places.indoor: inside a room: a library, a workshop, a hall
places.snow: snowy and frozen whatever the calendar says; the setting counts as winter
places.pool: a swimming pool, indoors or out
